stories.title: Meta ships Muse Realtime Avatar: a real-time avatar model distilled 60x (120 to 2 NFEs) for infinite conversational video
stories.summary: Meta released Muse Realtime Avatar, an audio-driven Diffusion Transformer that turns Muse Realtime Voice into expressive, live interactive avatars by consuming the same speech VQ token stream. The engineering headline is the distillation: a 40-step three-way-CFG teacher (120 model evaluations per chunk) is distilled via self-forcing plus distribution matching into an unguided two-step causal student (120 to 2 NFEs, ~60x), with a fixed-length KV cache carrying motion context forward for as long as the conversation runs. Meta reports 448x768 at 25 fps, ~870 ms turn latency and 12 concurrent sessions per GB200. Caveat: the reported preference wins over Runway Characters and HeyGen LiveAvatar come from a short live-call rater study, not a public benchmark, and the blog's examples are not all inside the shipped Muse app.

source.name: Meta AI Research - Bringing Your Muse to Life

stories.title: CFTC staff FAQ update: futures brokers and clearinghouses can hold customer funds in tokenized forms and keep blockchain recordkeeping
stories.summary: The CFTC issued updated staff FAQs on crypto-asset and blockchain registrant activity. The new Q12-Q15 let futures commission merchants and derivatives clearing organizations invest customer funds in tokenized forms of Regulation 1.25 permitted investments when the legal and economic rights are equivalent, and treat blockchain/DLT as satisfying the Regs 1.31 and 45.2 recordkeeping requirements (including foregoing separate off-chain copies as long as records can be produced even during network disruptions). It is a staff FAQ, not a Commission rule. For builders the signal is the center of gravity for U.S. crypto market structure moving into the agencies now that the CLARITY Act stalled in the Senate; the FAQ builds on Letters 25-39 and 26-05.

stories.title: Alloc Init publishes 'Shielded Bitcoin': a Zcash-style metaprotocol for private L1 transfers with no soft fork
stories.summary: Alloc Init (Shikhelman, Komarov, Moskvin) published Shielded Bitcoin, a metaprotocol for private Bitcoin L1 transfers with no soft fork and no trusted operators. Transaction data lands on Bitcoin; independent indexers verify ZK proofs and nullifiers, and peg-in/out is planned via PIPEs v2 witness encryption. It is a research proposal, not deployed code. For builders this is a credible path to L1 privacy without consensus changes. Caveat: peg-in/out is explicitly a later paper, witness encryption is experimental, and Bitcoin nodes do not enforce the metaprotocol.

quality.note: Open PDF paper plus official @BitcoinMagazine post; the paper exposes no machine-readable timestamp, so the X post time (17:31:19 UTC) is used. Medium confidence because it is a proposal, not deployed code.

stories.title: Google Research publishes a multi-agent 'video co-director' framework for coherent long-form video (Co-Director, CANVAS)
stories.summary: Google Research released an orchestration-layer framework that treats minutes-long, multi-shot video generation as a global optimization and world-state-tracking problem, built on top of Gemini and Veo. It bundles Co-Director (to appear at COLM 2026) for creative-intent search, CANVAS (to appear at EMNLP 2026) for persistent visual world-state, A2RD and VQQA, with a closed-loop MLLM judge to catch identity drift and cascading pipeline failures. It is a research/orchestration layer, not a new foundation video model. Caveat: the claimed 'substantial gains' are paper-level and qualitative rather than a public leaderboard.

stories.title: NVIDIA and Google DeepMind release an open protein-complex prediction dataset for 2,800+ viruses
stories.summary: A Google DeepMind/EMBL-EBI/NVIDIA coalition released an open dataset of predicted protein complexes across 2,800+ viruses, with roughly 30% of the interactions not present in the PDB, plus an open BioNeMo structure-prediction pipeline so others can run the sequence-to-structure inference. It is predictions, not crystal structures, and uses an AlphaFold2-era model rather than a new folding architecture. For builders the open pipeline and viral-interaction coverage are the usable part. Caveat: entries are confidence-labeled predictions, not experimental structures.

stories.title: Perplexity ships Photon: a Rust retrieval/ranking engine behind new Fast Search, p95 under 230 ms at $1 per 1k requests
stories.summary: Perplexity replaced its prior open-source retrieval engine with a new Rust retrieval and ranking stack called Photon, behind a new Fast Search tier. The company reports p95 under 230 ms (median 160 ms) and a -68% per-task cost on six internal agent benchmarks, priced at $1 versus $5 per 1k requests; Photon itself dropped p99 from ~800 ms to ~65 ms with -20% serving machines and 2.5x data/document capacity. Caveat: all latency and cost figures are Perplexity-internal, and the company reports Fast Search is -0.24 relevance and -3 pp answer-availability on its long-tail tests.

Caveat: it is a company statement, not a completed forensic report, and the root cause has not been published.

stories.title: Nature: two papers recast the fruit-fly protein Lsp2 as a nutrient-sensing link from diet to lifespan
stories.summary: Two Nature papers (with a matching News & Views) show that the Drosophila storage protein Lsp2 links mTORC1 to target-mRNA translation and, in a second paper, links early-life diet to adult translation and lifespan, recasting dietary restriction as a nutrient-sensing -> translation-control -> lifespan mechanism in development and adulthood. This is animal (Drosophila) evidence, not a human intervention, and it is a mechanism result rather than a therapeutic. For builders the significance is a named, testable handle on how nutrient sensing gates translation that may be conserved. Caveat: all results are in fruit flies; no human data is presented.

stories.title: NIH launches 'Linked Discoveries,' an experimental PubMed tool mapping related work and replications across ~29M papers
stories.summary: NIH launched Linked Discoveries, an experimental tool layered over roughly 29 million PubMed papers that maps related work including replications, with a same-day Science editorial on replication. It is research infrastructure, not a finding. For longevity/biotech builders it lowers the cost of checking whether a claimed intervention has independent support before you build on it. Caveat: the tool 'does not judge study quality or determine whether a finding has been replicated,' and NLM says the first public version will change with feedback.
